jobs.description:
Location:
Bay Area, California
Status:
Full-Time, Exempt
Type:
Remote-Based, with regular on-site work and travel among hotel properties throughout Northern California
Pay Range:
$145,000 to $155,000 per year, plus performance-based incentive
Reports To:
CEO / President

About Zenique Hotels
Zenique Hotels is a Bay Area hospitality ownership and management company that combines operational excellence, exceptional guest experiences, and a people-first culture.
We're one of the first hotel owner-operator groups to deploy autonomous AI agents across our portfolio. We use technology to answer guest calls, support reservations, and streamline operations so our teams can focus on what matters most: delivering memorable guest experiences. AI isn't a side project here. It's core to how we operate and how we intend to grow.

The Opportunity
Zenique is seeking a Regional Director of Operations to lead operational performance across its growing portfolio and support the company's transition back to self-managed hotel operations. This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for financial performance, guest satisfaction, operational consistency, and leadership effectiveness across multiple properties.

The Future You’ll Help Build
What sets this role apart is the opportunity to create Zenique’s operational playbook and build a genuinely AI-enabled hotel operation rather than inherit an established way of working. You’ll develop the systems, standards, and practices that will guide how our hotels operate as the portfolio grows.You'll lead the thoughtful integration of AI tools and autonomous agents into daily operations, helping define what modern, technology-forward hospitality looks like at Zenique in close partnership with the CEO.

What You'll Own
AI Enablement & Innovation 

Lead the adoption of AI-enabled tools and autonomous agents across hotel operations, in partnership with Zenique's technology partners, treating AI as a core driver of performance.
Translate operating needs into technology requirements, and build the SOPs, knowledge bases, and human escalation points that make AI-enabled services reliable.
Monitor AI-enabled processes for accuracy, guest satisfaction, cost savings, and service quality, and coach hotel leaders to use automation and operational data effectively.
Establish responsible-use standards that protect guest information, employee data, and service quality.

Portfolio Operations & Oversight

Conduct regular property visits and operational reviews; identify risks and gaps and drive timely corrective action.
Serve as the primary operational liaison between ownership, General Managers, brand representatives, and vendors.
Support hotel openings, renovations, conversions, and transitions.

Financial Performance

Own portfolio-level financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, and business planning.
Drive results across key metrics, including occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, GOP, and labor costs, developing action plans when performance falls short.
Provide ownership with clear, timely reporting on portfolio performance and improvement opportunities.

Guest Experience

Set and monitor portfolio-wide service standards and hold teams accountable for delivering them at every stage of the guest experience.
Review guest satisfaction scores, reviews, and loyalty data; partner with GMs on sustainable service improvements.
Balance technology and automation with the personal, human service that defines exceptional hospitality.

General Manager Leadership & People

Recruit, onboard, coach, and evaluate General Managers; set clear goals, scorecards, and development plans.
Build leadership capability in financial management, revenue strategy, operational discipline, and technology adoption.
Partner with the Head of People Operations on staffing, succession planning, performance management, and a people-first culture.

Brand Standards, Compliance & Risk

Ensure each hotel meets brand standards, franchise requirements, and company operating policies.
Lead preparation for quality-assurance inspections and resolve brand deficiencies.
Maintain internal controls and operational compliance related to safety, security, data privacy, and risk management.

What We're Looking For
10+ years of progressive hotel operations experience, including leadership of multiple properties or a complex full-service or select-service hotel.
Prior experience as a Regional Director of Operations, Area Director, General Manager, or comparable multi-property hospitality leader.
Experience overseeing hotels affiliated with Marriott, Wyndham, IHG or comparable brands.
Strong command of hotel financials, including budgeting, forecasting, labor management, revenue strategy, and performance metrics.
Demonstrated success improving profitability, guest satisfaction, and leadership effectiveness.
Genuine curiosity about technology, with hands-on experience implementing hotel systems, automation, or AI-enabled tools, and the conviction that technology and great hospitality reinforce each other.
Proven ability to coach and hold General Managers accountable while building trusted, collaborative relationships.
Strong analytical, project-management, and change-management skills, with the ability to balance strategy and hands-on execution.
Comfort in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment with evolving priorities.
Ability to travel regularly among Northern California properties (approximately 20%), and to respond to urgent operational matters outside regular business hours when reasonably necessary.

Benefits
Competitive compensation and benefits, plus a performance-based incentive opportunity.
Flexible PTO and flexible work arrangements when not traveling to or working from hotel properties.
Access to emerging AI and hotel technology solutions.

Leading a team of brand professionals, the Executive Director is responsible for the full spectrum of brand expression: integrated storytelling, LTO and campaign commercialization, always-on social ecosystem, and digital-first activations that transform cultural moments into paced business growth. This position builds campaigns designed for social amplification, engagement, and measurable business impact. The Executive Director serves as the strategic bridge between brand positioning, cultural relevance, and performance marketing, translating brand equity into financial outcomes that drive SSS growth, new guest acquisition, and long-term brand health. This position leads a team of brand professionals, developing associates to elevate their performance in support of the company’s growth goals.

Builds and develops a high-performing team of brand professionals, including national promotions leaders, social strategists, creator partnership managers, and content producers, fostering a culture of creative risk-taking balanced with business discipline and clear accountability to performance outcomes. We are currently seeking a Managing Director, Transition Management Executive
to join our team in Plano, Texas (US-TX), United States (US).

Company Overview

NTT DATA is a trusted global innovator of business and technology services, serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. We help clients innovate, optimize, and transform for long-term success through consulting, industry solutions, business process services, digital and IT modernization, and managed services.

As a Global Top Employer, we have diverse experts in more than 50 countries and a robust partner ecosystem of established and start-up companies. NTT DATA is seeking a highly experienced Managing Director, Transition Management Executive

This executive will serve as the single point of integration across multiple delivery towers, ensuring infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, enterprise applications, business process services, data, and managed services teams operate through a unified transition strategy and execution plan.

Working in close partnership with Integrated Delivery Leaders, Enterprise Architects, Organizational Change Management (OCM) leaders, and client executives, this individual will establish a "One NTT DATA" view of transition delivery, providing governance, transparency, risk management, and executive-level communication throughout the engagement lifecycle.

Lead transition strategy and execution for large-scale, multi-tower IT services engagements.
Establish and maintain a single integrated transition roadmap across all delivery workstreams.
Drive program governance, milestone management, resource planning, and KPI tracking.
Provide executive leadership throughout transition, transformation, and onboarding phases.

Integrated Program Management

Consolidate individual plans from infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, application, data, and business process services teams into a comprehensive master program plan.
Create visibility into cross-functional dependencies, critical path activities, and resource requirements.
Ensure alignment between transition deliverables and business objectives.
Manage enterprise-wide transition timelines and readiness assessments.

Architecture and Business Readiness Alignment

Partner closely with Enterprise Architects to align technical deployment sequencing with the approved solution architecture.
Collaborate with Organizational Change Management teams to ensure business adoption and user readiness plans support transition objectives.
Validate that organizational readiness activities align with technical implementation milestones.

Executive Governance and Stakeholder Management

Act as a trusted advisor to client executives and internal leadership teams.
Facilitate executive steering committees and governance forums.
Present transition status, risks, mitigation plans, and readiness updates to C-suite stakeholders.
Translate complex technical concepts into meaningful business outcomes and executive messaging.

Risk and Dependency Management

Identify, assess, and mitigate transition risks across multiple delivery towers.
Resolve scheduling conflicts, resource constraints, and interdependent workstream challenges.
Establish proactive escalation mechanisms and corrective action plans.
Ensure transition execution remains aligned to contractual commitments, financial objectives, and delivery milestones.

Sales and Pursuit Support

Support strategic pursuits and major deal cycles by contributing transition and mobilization strategies.
Participate in client presentations, workshops, and solution reviews.
Strengthen pursuit credibility by demonstrating operational readiness and delivery governance capabilities.
Partner with sales, solutioning, and delivery teams to develop transition management approaches for complex engagements.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Master's degree, MBA, or equivalent executive-level education preferred.

Experience

15+ years of experience leading large-scale enterprise IT services programs, transitions, or transformation initiatives.
Proven success managing multi-million-dollar, multi-tower technology engagements.
Experience integrating diverse delivery functions into a single enterprise transition plan.
Demonstrated success working alongside senior account leaders, architects, delivery executives, and client stakeholders.
Experience supporting strategic pursuits, large deal transitions, and complex service transformations.

Infrastructure services

Proven ability to navigate and lead within highly matrixed organizations.
Strong business acumen and customer-centric mindset.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.
Demonstrated success leading through complexity, ambiguity, and organizational change.

SAFe, Agile, or Transformation certifications

Solution Tree seeks a Chief Operating Officer to turn company strategy into coordinated execution across a complex, mission-driven education enterprise. The COO will be the CEO's principal operating partner, aligning leaders, priorities, resources, systems, and accountability so guidance becomes measurable outcomes. This is not a command-and-control role. Success depends on influence, judgment, relationships, disciplined follow-through, and the ability to lead strong functional executives without taking over their work. Think hurdle remover: the focus is execution.

The COO provides enterprise-wide coordination across Solution Tree, Marzano Resources, Solution Tree Canada, Results Coaching Global, state offices, and affiliated growth businesses and initiatives. The role spans publishing, professional development, events, educational technology, author and associate relations, customer operations, fulfillment, facilities, information technology, cybersecurity, state-office operations, coaching services, and enterprise project execution.

What We Can Achieve Together

The Director of Philanthropy Operations is responsible for directing the Florida Business Unit (BU) Development Operations Team in support of the annual Florida Fundraising Strategy as set by the Florida Director of Philanthropy and Florida Executive Director. The Director of Philanthropy Operations is responsible for co-creating a vision for the Philanthropy Operations team with the Florida Director of Philanthropy, directing all aspects of the four key strategic areas within the Florida development program; donor engagement and events, donor communications, major gift management, and philanthropy operations (gift coding/research/administration/project management). They will manage a team that handles gift processing, fundraising and financial reporting, events and trips, research, prospect management activity, donor engagement and stewardship, volunteer management, and pipeline building. During fundraising campaigns, they collaborate with BU leadership and direct the operations of the BU’s comprehensive campaign, ensuring that the campaign operating plan, timeline, deliverables and desired fundraising targets are met.

The Director of Philanthropy Operations will drive effective management and processes for all four areas of philanthropy operations with the overall objective of optimal support to maximize essential fundraiser time “out the door.” They will hold their direct reports accountable to achieve Philanthropy Operations measurable goals and objectives as set by the annual fundraising strategy and plan with the Director of Philanthropy.

We’re Looking For You

We’re looking for a passionate, dedicated person to lead our Chapter and work within our division. Systems Leadership, creativity, and implementing and developing strategic goals are key in this role. Come join TNC and apply today!

Essential Functions

The Director of Philanthropy Operations proactively works towards meeting the strategic priorities of the program by designing, developing and coordinating plans and related tactics and overseeing all day-to-day tasks of development operations. They work closely with the Director of Philanthropy to set measurable goals and metrics for programmatic success, building a strong donor/prospect pipeline, increasing accountability and building a fundraising program that can meet and exceed market potential. They manage a team responsible for principal and major gifts fundraising support, direct accurate and timely gift processing, and following processes to ensure maximum fundraising effectiveness. They oversee donor/prospect pipeline development and efforts to build strong principal and major gift portfolios. They manage prospect research, prospect assignments, fundraiser activity accountability and effective portfolio management. The Director of Philanthropy Operations aligns fundraising and program activities to ensure all prospect management and solicitation activities are coordinated, strategic, and donor-centered in approach. They ensure that solicitations meet TNC standards, increase flexibility of funding and that donor designations are honored through the revenue allocation review process.

They oversee all events and event staff, ensuring that events and trips follow TNC protocols, “best in class” standards, and add strategic value/PG & MG pipeline building necessary for increasing fundraising year over year, contributing the highest ROI possible for fundraising success. They will help create compelling programmatic content and effective and innovative events to achieve long-term fundraising goals. The Director of Philanthropy Operations works with development and chapter leadership to ensure alignment, teamwork and teambuilding, management and staff empowerment that fosters a positive and inclusive environment. The Director will work with teams to establish and track measures and lead indicators of progress and success, such as BU PPI and PbD Continuum tracking. They will serve as key team member for the enhancement of systems and tools used by the team, including new, innovative tools such as AI, advanced wealth screening, and communication innovation. The Director will reinforce consistency in the organization's policies and procedures and provide direction related to their relevant field(s). They are responsible for ensuring programmatic work is a collaborative and well-integrated effort within philanthropy, including organizing internal communications for their area. They will lead various activities, develop complex processes, project outcomes, and initiate solutions to improve effectiveness. Broad, proactive management responsibility for four or more administrative or professional staff, including training, professional development, establishing clear expectations, setting “stretch” objectives, and overseeing the execution of day-to-day work.
Commit actions and resources in a way that affects public image and binds the organization financially or legally.
Develop and administer budget, evaluate results and develop corrective strategies as needed.
Ensure that programmatic commitments, TNC policies and procedures, and financial standards are met and managed for ethical compliance.
Implement and direct multiple projects, directing work of staff, setting deadlines, and ensuring accountability.
Lead new programs/initiatives that will ensure department and organization-wide goals and strategies are achieved.
Maintain confidentiality of frequently sensitive and emotionally charged information.
Manage strategic initiatives through collaboration with stakeholders in order to enhance performance in accordance with short and long-term objectives.
Maximum opportunity to act independently resolves complex issues within program area.
May direct or participate in negotiations for complex, high profile or sensitive agreements.
Minimize legal risk to the Conservancy and ensure legal compliance with applicable state and local regulations.
Responsibility and accountability for meeting strategic goals and objectives.
Travel frequently and on short notice, work long hours and weekends.
Work environment involves only infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.

Bachelor’s degree and 7 years related experience.
Experience in planning and delivering budgetary responsibilities.
Experience managing and supervising a multidisciplinary team.
Experience developing, managing, and implementing multiple projects and strategic goals.
Experience working across complex organizations.
Experience working with cross-functional teams across multiple organizational levels.
Experience, coursework, or other training in principles, practices, and procedures of relevant field.

Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.
Effective training skills.
Effectively communicates via presentations, conversations, and documents.
Experience managing a geographically dispersed team.
Expert knowledge of current and evolving trends in relevant discipline.
Proficiency in synthesizing materials from multiple sources into a coherent and accurate summary.
Proficiency in working independently as well as jointly with colleagues on a team.
Understanding of best practices in non-profit management.

. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!
